query: What drives customer satisfaction (Overall Rating) across the different airlines?

per_column.name: Avg_Sub_Rating
per_column.rationale: A mean of the existing sub-rating columns gives a compact composite axis to correlate against Overall Rating. Somewhat redundant with the individual sub-ratings but adds genuine aggregate leverage, and values are a sound arithmetic derivation from present columns.

per_column.name: Satisfaction_Gap
per_column.rationale: Plausibly Overall Rating minus a sub-rating aggregate — a useful diagnostic of over/under-performance relative to details. Values are computable from present numeric columns, though the exact formula is opaque and it partly restates the target variable, slightly reducing independent value.

per_column.name: Pain_Point_Dimension
per_column.rationale: Identifying the worst-scoring dimension is a strong new axis for what drags ratings down. But evidence rows contradict the label: a review that praised inflight entertainment ('far better than any equivalent flights') is tagged pain point = Inflight Entertainment, and the reservation-system complaint maps to Value For Money without clear basis. The assignments are not reliably a sound reading of the text/scores.

per_column.name: Delight_Driver_Dimension
per_column.rationale: Best-scoring dimension is analytically valuable for identifying satisfaction drivers. However evidence undermines groundedness: a review complaining the 'regional seat was really uncomfortable' is tagged Delight Driver = Seat Comfort, directly contradicting the source text.

per_column.name: Sub_Rating_Variance
per_column.rationale: Dispersion across sub-ratings captures inconsistent experiences, a genuine new modeling axis distinct from the mean. Computable directly from existing sub-rating columns.

per_column.name: Service_Tier
per_column.rationale: A three-level bucket offers a convenient grouping variable, though it is largely a coarsening of Staff Service / composite ratings, limiting novelty. Mostly a sound categorisation of present ratings, though one sample ('no offer of pre departure drinks... nothing offered for 2.5 hours' rated Medium) is borderline.

per_column.name: Value_For_Money_Class_Adjusted
per_column.rationale: Adjusting value-for-money by travel class is a meaningful axis for comparing satisfaction fairly across cabins. Derivable from Value For Money + Class columns, though the adjustment logic is opaque and some mappings are hard to verify from the text.

judge.rationale: The numeric-derivative columns (Avg_Sub_Rating, Sub_Rating_Variance, Satisfaction_Gap, Value_For_Money_Class_Adjusted, Service_Tier) are well grounded in existing rating columns and give distinct, useful axes for modeling what drives Overall Rating. The two dimension-attribution columns (Pain_Point_Dimension, Delight_Driver_Dimension) are the most analytically pointed but show clear contradictions with the source text in multiple evidence samples, indicating unreliable attribution. This pulls the table-level groundedness down while usefulness stays reasonably high.
